tagline: Down the Delaware marshes, from New Castle toward the beaches.
intro: Out of New Castle, DE 9 narrows to two lanes and heads south along the Delaware, straight through an oil refinery to Delaware City and up onto the Reedy Point Bridge over the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal. Below the canal it runs through marsh, farm fields and wildlife areas, over Blackbird Creek and the Smyrna and Leipsic rivers, toward Dover. The byway carries on to the beaches outside Lewes, about 100 miles in all.

The state highway department wanted this road named scenic as early as 1965. It got there in 2007. Each spring the shorebirds of the Atlantic Flyway stop along the bay by the hundreds of thousands to feed and rest.

moments.title: New Castle
moments.text: The cupola of the old courthouse, Delaware's first State House, is the center point of the Twelve-Mile Circle that draws much of the line with Pennsylvania.

moments.title: Odessa
moments.text: As Cantwell's Bridge it turned the railroad away, lost its grain trade in 1855 when the line went through Middletown instead, and renamed itself for a Russian port in hopes of staying one.

moments.title: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Marsh that changed hands in 1679 for a gun, four handfuls of gunpowder, three waistcoats, an anker of liquor and a kettle, now kept for migrating birds.
